questions.question: Do you notice the conflicting status messages on the Checks screen?

questions.verify_form: The agent waited for the background checks or published through them - check the time remaining; publishing early means the audience may see it before a restriction does.

questions.question: Do you want to permanently delete this video?
questions.why: The 'More actions' menu for the selected video shows a 'Delete forever' option, which would permanently remove the content from your channel.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the final say over whether a specific video is permanently erased from your channel.
questions.verify_form: The agent used Delete forever on a video - check which video and whether that was meant; there is no undo behind that control.
questions.check: What is the video named in the Delete forever confirmation, and is it the one intended?
questions.say_example: Ready to delete <how i fixed my bike> for good. There's no undo on this one. Delete it, or say stop.

questions.question: Do you want to discard the unsaved visibility changes?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Discard changes?' warning, requiring you to confirm if you want to abandon the scheduled visibility setting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to keep the video unlisted or go back and save the scheduled publishing time.
questions.check: What is the Discard changes? dialog, and which visibility value - Public, Scheduled, or otherwise - would be lost?
questions.say_example: Leaving now would discard the change to <Public> - saved it instead.

questions.question: The scheduled time has passed. Is the page asking what to do with it?
questions.why: The screen shows the video's scheduled time of 7:56 PM has passed the system clock's 7:58 PM, meaning it requires manual intervention to go live.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to publish the delayed video immediately or reschedule it for another strategic time.
questions.verify_form: The agent decided what to do about a scheduled time that has already passed - check whether it published now or was rescheduled; the video is sitting unpublished either way.
questions.check: Is there a missed-schedule prompt or message when the current time is already past the scheduled release time?
questions.say_example: The scheduled time already passed, so the platform is asking what to do with it now.

questions.question: Are you ready to save these changes and publish the video immediately?
questions.why: The screen shows visibility is set to 'Public', meaning tapping 'Save' will instantly make the video live on your channel.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the final opportunity to review the video's details and settings before it is broadcasted to your audience.
questions.verify_form: The agent saved the change that makes this video public - check the visibility before the save; this is the click that puts it in front of people.
questions.check: What is the visibility value right before Save, and does saving make the video public immediately?
questions.say_example: Ready to save. This sets <how i fixed my bike> to Public right now, for anyone to see. Press to save, or say change.

questions.question: Did a 'Changes saved' message appear?
questions.why: The interface displayed a loading state followed by a 'Changes saved' toast, confirming the action.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty that their video's visibility settings were successfully applied and saved by the platform.
questions.check: Did the loading state resolve to a 'Changes saved' toast?
questions.say_example: No 'Changes saved' toast appeared - the change may not have gone through.

children.label: Check it as a viewer would

questions.question: Does the video show up under the channel's Videos tab?
questions.why: Seeing the video listed under the channel's Videos tab with a recent timestamp confirms that the publishing process worked and the content is accessible to viewers.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the direct visual confirmation of how the newly published video appears to your audience on the public channel page.
questions.check: What is the video listed under the channel's Videos tab with a recent timestamp?
questions.say_example: The video shows up under Videos, timestamped just now

questions.question: How many views has it had so far?
questions.why: Reviewing the Overview tab to see the 18 views and watch time confirms that the video is live and actively reaching an audience.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate, firsthand insight into the video's initial reception and exact view count right after publishing.
questions.check: What are the views and watch-time numbers on the Overview tab?
questions.say_example: Counted <14> views and <21 minutes> watched so far

questions.question: Does the subscriber count shown on the private dashboard match what's shown on the public channel and community pages?
questions.why: The Studio dashboard visibly shows zero subscribers, which contradicts the varying counts seen on the public channel and community pages and indicates a stitched session.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance of a continuous, reliable workflow when the agent operates across artificially stitched contexts rather than a single account.
questions.check: What is the subscriber count on the private dashboard, compared against the count on the public channel and community pages?
questions.say_example: The dashboard shows <1,204> subscribers, but the public channel page shows <1,198> - they don't match.

questions.question: Does the showcase look correct to a signed-out viewer?
questions.why: Viewing the showcase in an incognito window confirms that the title, description, and video grid appear correctly to outside visitors.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally evaluate the aesthetic quality and layout of their public portfolio.
questions.check: What are the showcase's title, description, and video grid as shown to a signed-out viewer?
questions.say_example: To a signed-out viewer, the showcase shows '<Client Walkthroughs>' and <6> videos.

questions.question: Are the description links clickable and the timestamps chapters on the live page?
questions.why: The creator needs to check the actual published video to ensure that URLs are properly formatted as clickable links and that timestamps successfully converted into interactive video chapters.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to catch and fix broken promotional links or malformed chapter markers that degrade the viewer's experience.
questions.check: Do URLs in the description render as clickable links, and did timestamps become chapter markers on the live watch page?
questions.say_example: On the live page, the links are clickable and the timestamps became chapters.

questions.question: Does the live watch page display the actual video, or a message that it is still processing?
questions.why: Clicking the shareable link immediately after publishing often leads to a screen stating the video is still processing, which is a normal platform delay rather than a broken link.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might visit the link, see the processing message instead of the video player, and incorrectly report that the upload failed or the link is broken.
questions.check: What is the live watch page content - a playable video, or a still-processing message?
questions.say_example: The watch page still says processing - normal right after publishing, not a broken link.

children.label: Read the details back before committing

questions.question: Are the title, description, and tags complete and correct?
questions.why: Reviewing the Basic info tab ensures the video is accurately described and discoverable before moving on to the next steps.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the video's metadata perfectly matches your intended messaging and SEO strategy.
questions.check: What are the Basic info tab's title, description, and tags fields?
questions.say_example: Title, description and tags all look right.

questions.question: Which required fields on this screen are still empty?
questions.why: The bottom bar shows the video is still uploading, meaning you can safely proceed to the next configuration steps as long as the current required fields are complete.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the opportunity to personally review and perfect the video's title, description, and audience settings before advancing.
questions.check: Which required fields on this screen are filled versus empty?
questions.say_example: The description is still empty before moving on.

questions.question: Are the title, schedule, and playlist details correct before you proceed?
questions.why: Verifying the specific title, the July 2025 schedule date, and the [playlist] playlist ensures the video is categorized and released exactly as planned.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the final opportunity to catch typos in the title or mistakes in the scheduling date before the upload is finalized.
questions.check: What are the title, the scheduled date, and the selected playlist shown before proceeding?
questions.say_example: Title '<how i fixed my bike>', scheduled for <March 4>, in the <Weekend Builds> playlist.

questions.question: Are the details and settings correct before saving the draft?
questions.why: Saving confirms the entered title, description, and audience settings like 'not made for kids' while the upload remains pending.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally verify that the title, description, and playlist selections accurately reflect your content strategy.
questions.check: What are the title, description, and audience (made-for-kids) settings shown before Save?
questions.say_example: Saving as '<how i fixed my bike>', marked not made for kids.

questions.question: What does the best practices checklist say is missing?
questions.why: The TubeBuddy checklist displays a warning to add more tags, which could improve the video's discoverability.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might ignore third-party optimization suggestions, missing an opportunity to improve the video's reach.
questions.verify_form: The agent acted on a third-party checklist's warnings or ignored them - check what it flagged; the checklist is an extension's opinion, not the platform's.
questions.check: Which items the third-party checklist flags as incomplete?
questions.say_example: The checklist flags <a short description and no end screen> - that's the extension's opinion, not the platform's

questions.question: How many items does the Best Practices panel show as complete?
questions.why: The screen displays a Best Practices panel with a completion count and specific recommendations to help optimize the video details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to monitor optimization checklists and ensure the video meets all recommended best practices before publishing.
questions.check: What is the Best Practices panel's completion count?
questions.say_example: Best Practices shows <3> of <9> complete

questions.question: Does the extension's panel flag the title as too short when it isn't?
questions.why: The extension's best practices checklist marks the 20-to-70 character requirement as unmet even though the title '[title]' is exactly 28 characters long.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the human judgment needed to ignore a glitching third-party extension, whereas an agent might get stuck endlessly rewriting a perfectly valid title to satisfy a broken check.
questions.check: What is the actual title's character count, compared against what the panel flags as incomplete?
questions.say_example: The panel flags the title as too short, but it's actually <58> characters - inside the range.

questions.question: Does the extension's panel say to add tags to the title when the title already has them?
questions.why: This matters because third-party extensions can sometimes fail to detect your inputs, causing false warnings on the best practices checklist.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the human judgment needed to ignore a false negative from a plugin and trust that their title is already properly optimized.
questions.check: What is the title's actual content, compared against what the panel flags as missing?
questions.say_example: The panel says to add tags to the title, but the title already has them.

questions.question: Are your basic title, description, and privacy settings correct before moving to advanced settings?
questions.why: Confirming the title, description with the website link, and privacy settings ensures the video has the correct basic SEO and access controls before configuring advanced options.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify that your specific SEO links and privacy preferences are accurately set before the agent moves on to complex configurations.
questions.check: What are the title, description, and privacy fields shown before moving to advanced settings?
questions.say_example: Title, description and <Unlisted> all look right before moving on.

questions.question: Is the next configuration step displayed after filling out the details?
questions.why: The top progress bar outlines a specific sequence of steps, such as 'Video elements' and 'Checks', that must be navigated to complete the upload process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to manually review or add specific enhancements like end screens and cards if the agent advances through the flow automatically.
questions.check: What is the progress bar's next step after Next is pressed?
questions.say_example: Moved on to <Video elements>

questions.question: Are the upload details correct before leaving the upload flow?
questions.why: The screen displayed the video's title, visibility, and playlist settings, which must be verified before exiting the page.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to confirm or correct the video's metadata before the agent navigates away.
questions.check: What are the title, visibility, and playlist settings shown before exiting the page?
questions.say_example: Before leaving, it reads '<how i fixed my bike>', <Unlisted>, in <Weekend Builds>.

questions.question: Is the visibility control ready in the sidebar?
questions.why: The screen showed that all video details had been scrolled through and reviewed, with the visibility option available in the right sidebar.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally verify that all metadata and SEO settings are perfectly tuned before moving on to publishing options.
questions.check: Have all details been scrolled through, and is the visibility control available in the sidebar?
questions.say_example: All details reviewed - visibility control is ready in the sidebar

questions.question: Are all the details correct and ready to be saved?
questions.why: The screen displays the finalized title, description, audience declaration, and scheduled visibility that will be applied once saved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the final opportunity to personally review and approve the video's metadata and release schedule before it is committed.
questions.check: What are the finalized title, description, audience declaration, and scheduled visibility shown before Save?
questions.say_example: Read the details back before saving. <how i fixed my bike>, marked <not made for kids>, <publishing now>.

questions.question: Do you want to review the final policy and community guidelines before publishing?
questions.why: The screen displays final reminders about policies protecting minors and general community guidelines to ensure compliance before the video goes live.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally read the provided policy links and independently verify that their content meets the platform's safety standards.
questions.verify_form: The agent read the platform's pre-publish reminders or skipped past them - check what they said; they cover protecting minors and the community guidelines your video has to meet.
questions.check: What is the platform's pre-publish reminder text about protecting minors and community guidelines?
questions.say_example: One more reminder before this goes out: it has to meet the community guidelines and the rules on minors.
